predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: Media, where Timarchus had been satrap since Antiochus IV's accession in 175 BC (without independent Atropatene)

successors.name: Seleucid Empire
successors.text: Media and Babylonia, recovered when 'Demetrius defeated and killed Timarchus in 160 BC'

ledger.x: 163 BCE: Timarchus, satrap of Media since 175, makes himself king.
163 BCE: Media leaves Seleucid rule under its satrap.
160 BCE: Demetrius I marches against him.
160 BCE: Demetrius defeats and kills Timarchus, and the Babylonians give him the title Soter.
160 BCE: Media and Babylonia return to the Seleucids.
160 BCE: the rebel kingdom ends with Timarchus's death; his brother Heracleides later 'avenged him and backed the pretender Alexander Balas'.

wars.name: Demetrius I's war against Timarchus
wars.outcome: Demetrius I defeated and killed Timarchus in 160 BC and 'dethroned Ariarathes, king of Cappadocia'; Rome indirectly supported those who wanted to divide the Seleucid Empire, Timarchus among them (the page's sense).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; Media and Babylonia are the regions named.
